Classmate Sun Rong, heiress of a powerful family, rescues him from bullies and falls for him; a summoning class produces Er-Ha, a talking Shiba Inu; and a legendary cultivator becomes his devoted follower. Wang Ling keeps quietly wrecking threats so someone else gets the credit. Ending: during a sabotaged inter-school contest, an assassin fatally wounds Sun Rong and Wang Ling's seal breaks. She is sent back from the underworld, he nearly remakes the world to save her, and Er-Ha's idea of reversing time restores the old world, wipes her memory and puts his power back under control.
114121.q: ⚠ No source discusses LGBTQ+ content; season 1's romance is straight. Its core is a boy who has to suppress his real self and feelings to pass as ordinary, and only acts as himself when someone he loves is at stake.
114121.g: One of the first Chinese donghua to reach a wide Western audience through Netflix and Crunchyroll, with an English dub, and it has run to several seasons. It parodies the cultivation genre: the usual grind to power becomes the problem of having too much power and just wanting to go to class.

98514.meta: 2018 · P.A. Works · TV, 13 episodes · original anime in Cygames' Umamusume franchise, dir. Kei Oikawa
98514.w: A world much like ours where famous Japanese racehorses of the past are reborn as "horse girls," girls with horse ears and tails and a racehorse's speed and stamina. The best train at Tracen Academy in Tokyo and race to become stars, and the winners perform as idols in a "Winning Live" concert after each race. Special Week, a country girl from Hokkaido raised by her adoptive mother, transfers to Tracen promising to become the best horse girl in Japan, and joins the scrappy Team Spica mostly because she idolizes her roommate Silence Suzuka. Every race mirrors a real career. Suzuka pulls far ahead in the Fall Tenno Sho but breaks her leg near the final stretch; while she recovers, Special Week neglects her own training to help her and keeps losing, until a trip home resets her. Ending: Special Week comes from the back in the Japan Cup to beat the French champion and keep her promise. In an extra episode Suzuka returns from America for the Dream Trophy race, and the season closes with everyone performing together, without saying who won.
98514.q: The cast is almost all women and the story runs on bonds between girls; its emotional center is Special Week's devotion to Silence Suzuka, her roommate, teammate, role model and best friend. The show presents it as friendship and rivalry, never romance, and men are nearly absent apart from the Trainer. ⚠ No critical or official source found discussing a queer or yuri reading. Cygames' official fan-work rules ask fans not to make sexual works, to protect its relationships with the real horses' owners, which in practice limits fan romance content.
98514.g: It turns real horse-racing history into an underdog sports drama: Suzuka's fracture is modeled on the real horse's career-ending injury, and the show lets her recover. Anime News Network praised its sports storytelling and characters while noting the mobile-game elements sometimes clash with the story. It launched one of Cygames' biggest franchises; the game followed in 2021.

117533.meta: 2021 · Liden Films · TV, 13 episodes · seinen spin-off manga by Shigemitsu Harada and Issei Hatsuyoshiya (2018–2021)
117533.w: Like the original Cells at Work!, it's set inside a human body drawn as a city, with the cells as workers. This body belongs to an unhealthy adult man who drinks, smokes, is stressed and doesn't sleep. The title borrows "black company," the Japanese term for an exploitative employer that works its staff to exhaustion. A rookie red blood cell, AA2153, makes oxygen deliveries through a collapsing workplace, while the white blood cell U-1196 and the immune cells fight infections they can't keep up with. Each episode is a health crisis handled with gore and grim humor. Ending: the man has a heart attack; a defibrillator and a stent save him, he quits smoking and drinking, and the cells recover. After the credits, a syringe pulls AA2153 and U-1196 into a new body in even worse shape.
117533.q: It swaps the genders of the original's leads: the red blood cells are now male and the white blood cells female (platelets stay little girls, Killer T cells stay burly men). ⚠ No source treats it as queer content. Anime Feminist called the swap mostly a novelty, criticized the female white cells' sexualized designs, and warned about the manga's sexualized violence against female characters.
117533.g: A critique of overwork and exploitative workplaces dressed up as a biology lesson. Anime News Network linked it to overwork in the anime industry itself; /Film called it an anime that will scare you into taking care of yourself. Anime Feminist praised its body horror and openly anti-capitalist themes while staying wary of how often it brutalizes its characters.

19775.meta: 2014 · Polygon Pictures · TV, 12 episodes (season 2, 2015) · seinen manga by Tsutomu Nihei
19775.w: The year 3394, a thousand years after the Gauna, shapeshifting aliens no one can communicate with, destroyed the solar system. What's left of humanity drifts through space on the seed ship Sidonia, built from Earth's remains, with a culture based closely on Japan's. Its people have been engineered to photosynthesize, so they barely need to eat, and they reproduce by cloning. Nagate Tanikaze, raised in secret in the ship's lowest levels by his grandfather on an old flight simulator, comes up to the surface after his grandfather dies, can't photosynthesize so he's always hungry, and is picked to pilot the legendary mech Tsugumori. His closest friend is Izana Shinatose, a fellow pilot from a third gender that developed during humanity's centuries in space. Another pilot, Shizuka Hoshijiro, dies saving Nagate, and a Gauna later appears that speaks in her voice. Ending: Nagate destroys that Hoshijiro-mimicking Gauna, his platoon destroys the larger Gauna, and he chooses to fight alongside a rival he can't forgive.
19775.q: Izana is one of the best-known intersex or third-gender characters in anime. The Japanese dialogue uses gender-neutral language for Izana; English versions often use "she." LezWatch.TV lists Izana as intersex and queer. Izana's body can adapt to a chosen partner, and Izana's love for Nagate makes it become female. ⚠ Not confirmed whether that happens in season 1 or 2. Scholar Roger Andre Søraa (Fafnir journal) reads Izana as a "post-gendered" body with "relational gender," argues the turn to female partly reinforces straight norms, and calls Nagate's attraction across genders and even species the show's subtler queering. He also notes gender doesn't limit who can pilot and the captain is an immortal woman.
19775.g: Netflix's first original anime (July 2014). Its full-CG production was unusual for TV anime, and Hideo Kojima praised it for reviving a sci-fi spirit. It mixes hard-SF worldbuilding (photosynthesizing humans, cloning, immortal leaders) with cosmic horror and real-robot combat where pilots die.

4898.meta: 2008–09 · A-1 Pictures · TV, 24 episodes · manga by Yana Toboso (2006–)
4898.w: Victorian London, with demons, angels and grim reapers mixed in. On his tenth birthday, Ciel Phantomhive's manor was attacked, his parents killed, and he was sold to a cult that abused him. To survive he made a contract with a demon, who serves him until his revenge is done and then gets to eat his soul. Ciel names the demon Sebastian Michaelis, after his dead dog, and Sebastian poses as his flawless butler. At twelve, Ciel is an earl, runs a toy company, and investigates London's underworld as the Queen's "Watchdog," with a comically inept staff who turn out to be trained killers. Early arcs include the Jack the Ripper case, where Ciel's aunt Madam Red and the reaper Grell Sutcliff are the killers. The final arc pits Ciel against Angela/Ash, one angel in female and male forms, who purges London with fire. Ending: on Tower Bridge, Sebastian takes his true demon form and destroys Angela/Ash. Ciel's revenge is done, and at a ruined mansion he tells Sebastian to make taking his soul painful. ⚠ The final arc is anime-original.
4898.q: Grell Sutcliff, a flamboyant red-clad reaper who insists on being treated as a lady, is widely read by fans as a trans woman and appears on lists of anime trans characters. The canon is contested: the anime uses male pronouns, and Toboso has switched between pronouns and called Grell "okama," a slur closer to "gay crossdresser." Grell is also played for comic relief and is a murderer, so the representation is valued and criticized at once. ⚠ A claim that the manga guide officially calls Grell transgender is unverified. Ciel goes undercover dressed as a girl in the Ripper arc, and Angela/Ash is one being with female and male forms. Sebastian/Ciel is a huge fan pairing.
4898.g: One of the defining gothic anime of the late 2000s. The manga has 36M+ copies in circulation, and the franchise has run to many more seasons and a 2014 live-action film. It's a Victorian detective story built on a Faustian bargain, with a child lead whose trauma, including the abuse he suffered, drives the plot.

129898.meta: 2021 · Silver Link / Studio Palette · TV, 12 episodes · light novel by Rui Tsukiyo
129898.w: The world's greatest assassin is betrayed by his own organization and killed just before he can retire. A goddess reincarnates him into a world of swords and magic on one condition: when he grows up, he must kill the Hero, who is prophesied to destroy the world. He's reborn as Lugh Tuatha Dé, heir of a baronial family that are secretly the kingdom's assassins, and combines modern knowledge (firearms, chemistry, business) with magic. He trains his childhood friend and magic teacher Dia, and rescues Tarte, a girl abandoned to die, and Maha, a girl from a trafficking ring, turning both into his team. Civil war breaks out in Dia's home region, and her own father asks Lugh's family to assassinate her to end it. Ending: Lugh and Dia's father fake her death, Lugh destroys the warrior Setanta with a magnetically launched tungsten round, the family adopts Dia, and the season closes on news that the real Hero, Epona, has arrived.
129898.q: Little, and at the edges. ⚠ The Hero, Epona, is registered as a man but is a woman; she appears only at the very end of season 1, so this detail is from the light novel. ⚠ In the anime, Lugh's mother dresses him in girls' clothes, possibly grieving a daughter she lost. Otherwise it's a standard straight harem.
129898.g: A cold-blooded isekai whose hero kills by planning, poison and sniping instead of power-ups. ANN praised the finale for setting up a hero-versus-monster showdown and then subverting it; other viewers found it rushed. Content notes: trafficking and drugs are part of the plot.
